options.summary:
Production is down for one reason only: the OpenAI org has no prepaid credit. OpenAI's error-codes page names this failure `credit_balance_exhausted`: "Your organization has no prepaid credits remaining." Its fix is "Add credits". Every call site already speaks OpenAI, and every quality baseline was measured on gpt-4o and gpt-4o-mini. That makes a top-up the fastest path to a working app for Apple review, with no code change.

Buy at least $50. The fetched rate-limits table puts "$50 paid" at Tier 2, which raises gpt-4o from 30,000 to 450,000 TPM and gpt-4o-mini from 200,000 to 2,000,000 TPM. At the runbook's corrected verdict cost of 6,500–6,800 TPM (prompt tokens plus the max_tokens reservation), the gpt-4o ceiling rises from about 4.4–4.6 verdicts/min to about 66–69/min (MODELLED). Tier 1 also has a $100/month usage limit, which is a second way to go down.

Modelled cost at the fetched prices ($2.50/$10 per 1M tokens for gpt-4o; $0.15/$0.60 for gpt-4o-mini; moderation "Free"):
- Cold compare: about $0.017–0.040.
- Warm compare: about $0.014–0.025.
- So $50 covers roughly 1,250–3,000 compares.

Turn on auto-recharge. Set an alert threshold, not a low hard spend cap: OpenAI's `organization_spend_limit_exceeded` is also a 429 and would bring back the same outage.

Railway settings from the runbook: OPENAI_MAX_RETRIES=1 and OPENAI_FALLBACK_MAX_RETRIES=0. The worst-case verdict chain drops from 6 attempts to 3. These need a RESTART. The runbook says the lazy clients pick the change up without one, but that is only true until each client is first built: all three client getters memoise, so only the per-call verdict fallback reads the env fresh. url_extraction_service builds its own client without max_retries and keeps the SDK default of 2 whatever the env says. Also set ENABLE_FULL_STREAM_DEADLINE=true; the runbook calls it "a hard pairing with OpenAI re-funding".

ENABLE_LLM_PREFLIGHT_BREAKER: keep it OFF for the smoke run. Before submitting, turn it ON only if Settings → Limits shows Tier 2 or higher. If the account is still on Tier 1, leave it OFF.
- The flag is read per call (no restart needed).
- It trips after 3 consecutive transient failures (429, 5xx, connection or timeout) and then refuses EVERY compare for 600 s with a 503 LLM_UNAVAILABLE.
- On Tier 1, one burst of TPM 429s could lock out an Apple reviewer for 10 minutes.
- On Tier 2 or higher it mainly protects against the next credit exhaustion or outage, and stops paid scraping spend on compares that would fail at the LLM anyway.
- The mobile app has no i18n key for LLM_UNAVAILABLE, so Arabic users would see the English message.

Verification is a gate before submission:
1. /health.
2. scripts/bundle_d_prod_smoke.py. It registers a real throwaway user in prod on every run, and its compare probe only shape-checks a cached pair, so it cannot catch a degraded verdict.
3. An uncached q= compare with explicit checks: HTTP 200, success true, no comparison.error, non-empty pros and cons.
4. The same on the SSE stream.
5. A real /image/identify.
6. Railway logs and the OpenAI Usage page show gpt-4o and gpt-4o-mini traffic with no 429s.
7. Then the pre-tested demo pairs on a device, in both en and ar.
steps: 0. PRECONDITION (Ahmed, 2 min): confirm which OpenAI org/project owns the key in Railway's `web` OPENAI_API_KEY. Match the key's name in platform.openai.com → API keys against the project; never print or paste the key value. The whole fix assumes the credits land in THAT org.

1. OPENAI DASHBOARD, READ FIRST (Ahmed): open Settings → Organization → Limits (the error-codes page links it as https://platform.openai.com/settings/organization/limits). Record in docs/runbooks/2026-09-02-openai-tpm-launch-sizing.md §1: the tier, the gpt-4o TPM/RPM, the gpt-4o-mini TPM/RPM, the monthly usage limit, and any enforced org or project spend limit, with the date. The runbook calls this 'a hard launch gate'.

2. OPENAI DASHBOARD, BILLING TOP-UP (Ahmed): go to Settings → Organization → Billing (https://platform.openai.com/settings/organization/billing, as linked from the credit_balance_exhausted entry) and add prepaid credits. Recommended: at least $50. The fetched rate-limits table lists Tier 2 at '$50 paid', which lifts gpt-4o TPM from 30,000 to 450,000. After purchase, re-open Settings → Limits and confirm the tier actually changed. Whether the tier upgrade or the credit balance is instant was not fetched (help.openai.com returned 403), so verify on the page rather than assume.

3. OPENAI DASHBOARD, AUTO-RECHARGE (Ahmed): on the same Billing page, enable auto-recharge with a threshold and a recharge amount; suggested threshold ≥ $20, recharge ≥ $50, sized from the modelled $0.017–0.040 per cold compare. The exact UI fields and minimums are UNFETCHED (the help article returned 403), so follow the page. Reason: the current outage IS an empty prepaid balance.

4. OPENAI DASHBOARD, ALERTS NOT HARD CAPS (Ahmed): in Settings → Limits, set a notification/alert threshold for spend. Do NOT set an enforced org or project spend limit near expected spend: 'organization_spend_limit_exceeded' and 'project_spend_limit_exceeded' are both 429s that reproduce the outage. Also note the monthly usage limit (Tier 1 = $100/month; Tier 2 = $500/month) and request a higher approved limit if launch traffic could reach it ('organization_usage_limit_exceeded').

5. RAILWAY `web` ENV (Ahmed, dashboard): set OPENAI_MAX_RETRIES=1 and OPENAI_FALLBACK_MAX_RETRIES=0 (runbook §3 launch settings; worst-case verdict chain = (1+1)+(1+0) = 3 attempts, down from 6, per model_config.verdict_chain_max_attempts). Also set ENABLE_FULL_STREAM_DEADLINE=true (runbook §4 hard pairing; bounds the post-Phase-1 stream verdict tail). Optionally set ENABLE_PREVERDICT_DISCONNECT_ABORT=true (runbook §4, 'complementary'). Leave ENABLE_PRICE_CACHE_WARMER false.

6. RESTART `web` AFTER STEP 5 (required, not optional): all three client getters memoise, so the lazy clients are not re-read after first use: openai_service.py module client (built at import, :34-38), the openai_service.get_client cache (_client_cache, :45-79) and extraction_service.get_client (_client, :58-77). Only the verdict fallback (extraction_service.py:2675-2678, with_options per call) reads the env fresh. The runbook's 'lazily-built clients ... pick it up without one' holds only before first construction. Confirm in the Railway dashboard that a new deployment went live, then GET /health = 200. A key rotation (a new OPENAI_API_KEY) also needs this restart; a top-up on the same key does not.

7. ENABLE_LLM_PREFLIGHT_BREAKER: keep it OFF for the verification in steps 8–13 so any failure shows the real error. After verification, turn it ON (read per call, no restart: api_budget_service.py:709-714) ONLY IF step 1/2 shows Tier ≥ 2. If still Tier 1, leave it OFF: the breaker trips after CB_FAILURE_THRESHOLD=3 consecutive transient failures (429 incl. TPM, 5xx, connection) and denies every compare for CB_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT=600 s with 503 LLM_UNAVAILABLE. At 30,000 gpt-4o TPM, one burst from a reviewer could lock the app for 10 minutes. Leave LLM_BREAKER_CACHE_TTL at its 60 s default.

8. VERIFY, SMOKE PACK (anyone with the repo): `python scripts/bundle_d_prod_smoke.py --verbose`. It needs exit 0. Caveats: it REGISTERS a real throwaway user in prod Supabase on every run, and its only compare probe (#12) is the CACHED pair 'iPhone 15 vs Samsung Galaxy S24', shape-checked for success/products/metadata keys only. It proves the parse leg now works (the current state is a 400) but NOT that the verdict is real.

9. VERIFY, UNCACHED TEXT COMPARE: GET https://web-production-58776.up.railway.app/api/v1/text/compare?q=<a pre-tested demo pair>&region=bahrain&nocache=true. Assert: HTTP 200; success == true; no `comparison.error` key (its presence means 'verdict generation unavailable', the degraded deterministic-template path); products[*] carry specs and pros/cons; the winner reason is non-empty. Repeat once with &lang=ar. Space the calls out: at Tier 1 the gpt-4o leg caps at ~4.4–4.6 verdicts/min (runbook, MODELLED).

10. VERIFY, STREAM: GET /api/v1/text/compare/stream?q=<a second pair>&nocache=true (SSE). Assert: no SSE `error` event (today the failure arrives as an `error` event on HTTP 200), the final result event arrives, and the verdict fields match step 9's checks.

11. VERIFY, CAMERA: POST /api/v1/image/identify as multipart `images` (1–4 real product photos). Assert HTTP 200 with identified products and the auto-compare; today's failure is HTTP 500 'Image analysis failed. Please try again.' because identify_products does not catch the 429.

12. VERIFY, LOGS AND USAGE (Ahmed, dashboards): Railway `web` logs for the verification window contain no '429', 'insufficient_quota', 'credit_balance_exhausted' or '[CIRCUIT]' lines. OpenAI Usage shows gpt-4o and gpt-4o-mini requests at the matching times, with cents of spend. Do not use metadata.total_cost as spend: it is computed with hardcoded gpt-4o-mini rates even for the gpt-4o verdict.

13. VERIFY, DEVICE: run the pre-tested demo pairs (en + ar) plus one camera compare on the actual build Apple will receive, pointed at the prod URL. Only then submit. If step 7 turned the breaker ON, repeat one compare afterwards to confirm it did not trip.

14. AFTER SUBMISSION (monitor): check the OpenAI balance and auto-recharge daily during the review window. Watch for 429s on Railway. If the tier is still 1 when reviewers are active, do not change model ids or add load; the runbook's fallback levers (verdict onto mini, or a verdict cache) are code or behaviour changes that need their own A/B before shipping.

options.effort_estimate: About 1.5–2.5 hours of Ahmed's time and zero engineering: dashboard read + top-up + auto-recharge + alerts ~30 min; Railway env + restart + /health ~10 min; smoke + uncached + stream + camera checks ~30–45 min; device run of the demo pairs in en/ar ~30 min. Cash: $50 recommended initial top-up (the Tier-2 threshold per the fetched table). At the MODELLED $0.017–0.040 per cold compare that is roughly 1,250–3,000 compares, far more than an App Review needs. No code change and no PR, apart from optionally recording the tier in the runbook §1 table.
risks: TIER-1 THROUGHPUT WALL: if the $50 does not move the org to Tier 2 (or the tier upgrade lags), gpt-4o stays at 30,000 TPM. At 6,500–6,800 TPM per verdict (runbook, measured prompt + max_tokens reservation) that is ~4.4–4.6 verdicts/min for the whole deployment. Two reviewers plus the founders' own demos can hit it, and the result is mid-compare 429s. Verify the tier in Settings → Limits before submitting.

RE-EXHAUSTION / SPEND CAPS: without auto-recharge the prepaid balance empties again (today's outage). A too-low enforced org or project spend limit, or the Tier-1 $100/month usage limit, fails the same way with a different 429 code (organization_spend_limit_exceeded / project_spend_limit_exceeded / organization_usage_limit_exceeded).

RESTART IS REQUIRED FOR THE RETRY KNOBS: the runbook and model_config comments say the lazy clients pick OPENAI_MAX_RETRIES up without a restart. They do only before first construction, since all three getters memoise. Setting the env without a redeploy silently keeps 2 retries (6 attempts per verdict in a 429 storm).

url_extraction_service.get_client passes no max_retries, so /url/compare and /url/extract keep the SDK default (2) whatever OPENAI_MAX_RETRIES says; the runbook's 'all four constructions' does not cover this fifth client.

BREAKER FALSE-TRIP: with ENABLE_LLM_PREFLIGHT_BREAKER ON, 3 consecutive transient failures (including TPM 429s, which are RateLimitError) deny every compare for 600 s with an English-only 503 message (the mobile app has no LLM_UNAVAILABLE i18n key). That is why the plan gates it on Tier ≥ 2.

SMOKE BLIND SPOT: scripts/bundle_d_prod_smoke.py checks only a cached compare's keys, so a degraded 200 (success:true with comparison.error and a template verdict) would pass. It also creates a real user row in prod on every run.

COST ACCOUNTING IS NOT SPEND: metadata.total_cost and the admin cost dashboards price every call, including the gpt-4o verdict, at hardcoded gpt-4o-mini rates. Use the OpenAI Usage page for real spend. At the fetched prices the gpt-4o verdict alone (5,498–5,942 input tokens × $2.50/1M ≈ $0.014–0.015, plus up to 1,000 output × $10/1M ≤ $0.01) outweighs the whole mini leg.

PRIVACY / APP REVIEW: the PDPL opt-out route (OPENAI_API_KEY_PRIVATE via select_client_for_user) has zero callers, so every user, opted out or not, goes through the shared project key, which the openai_service.get_client docstring describes as the 'data-sharing project'. If the App Store privacy labels or the privacy policy promise opt-out routing, that promise is not implemented. Reconcile the wording before submission; a top-up does not fix it.

SECRET HYGIENE: extraction_service.get_client logs the API key's last 10 characters at INFO on first build (extraction_service.py:~65), so the post-restart Railway logs will contain a key fragment. Do not paste those logs into transcripts or issues.

LOCAL-VS-LOCK SDK DRIFT: the lock pins openai==3.3.1 (requirements.txt:97), but the SDK's 429 retry and x-should-retry semantics were only read on a local 2.21.0; how 3.3.1 treats an insufficient_quota 429 (retry or not) is unmeasured.

UNFETCHED: the auto-recharge UI fields, the minimum purchase, the credit-activation delay and credit expiry (help.openai.com returned HTTP 403). Also unfetched: whether the Tier-2 '$50 paid' qualification carries a waiting period (the fetched table shows only the dollar threshold). Treat all of these as 'verify on the page'.

verdict_chain_max_attempts() = (1 + openai_max_retries()) + (1 + openai_fallback_max_retries()); defaults 2 and inherit, so 6; unset or blank env falls back to the default; negatives clamp to 0.

The openai_service module-level client reads max_retries at import. get_client caches in _client_cache, and extraction_service.get_client caches in the global _client. Only the verdict fallback reads openai_fallback_max_retries per call via with_options. So in practice a restart is needed for OPENAI_MAX_RETRIES.
url_extraction_service.get_client builds AsyncOpenAI with api_key, base_url and timeout only, with no max_retries, so it always uses the SDK default and ignores OPENAI_MAX_RETRIES.
ENABLE_LLM_PREFLIGHT_BREAKER is read per call (os.getenv at every check) and defaults OFF. With the flag OFF, guarded_llm_create is a bare chat.completions.create.

The breaker trips at CB_FAILURE_THRESHOLD=3 consecutive failures, with CB_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT=600 s and CB_HALF_OPEN_MAX_CALLS=1. RateLimitError, APIConnectionError, InternalServerError, 5xx and TimeoutError count as transient failures; a bare cancellation records none.

When the breaker short-circuits, the compare returns success:false, code 'LLM_UNAVAILABLE', and the copy 'Still warming up the comparison engine — give it another tap in a moment.'. text_routes maps it to 503. The mobile app has no i18n key for it, so the English string renders verbatim.

verdicts.reasoning:
This is partly right. Most of it is in the source, but the 4.4–4.6 verdicts/min figure depends on an assumption that OpenAI's own page does not support, and the arithmetic is slightly off.

CONFIRMED:
(1) docs/runbooks/2026-09-02-openai-tpm-launch-sizing.md (main) line 21 reads "| Account tier | _unverified_ |". Lines 6-7 say "The account's real tier is **UNKNOWN** — verifying it is a hard launch gate, not an optional step."
(2) The row at line 47 has the CORRECTED 2026-09-07 note. It says build_verdict_prompt "tokenises to 5,498–5,942 prompt tokens over the recorded fixtures (measured twice, independently)" and that max_tokens=1000 gives "4.4–4.6 verdicts/min (5.2/min if the reservation premise is discarded)". It also says "verdict_chain_max_attempts() resolves to 6 in prod (both retry knobs unset)". These numbers are the doc's own; I did not re-measure them.
(3) Code check. In app/services/model_config.py (main), _SDK_DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES = 2 (line 169). verdict_chain_max_attempts() returns (1+openai_max_retries())+(1+openai_fallback_max_retries()), and its docstring says "Shipped default: (1+2)+(1+2) = 6". So if both env vars are unset, the result is 6. I did not check whether they are unset on Railway: that would need a Railway tool, which is forbidden here. The doc is the only source for "in prod".
(4) max_tokens=1000 is real. extraction_service.py on main sets it through token_limit_kwargs(verdict_model, 1000) at lines 2640 and 2685 (also 1580). The doc's ':2447' citation is out of date.
(5) The Tier-1 limit is confirmed by vendor text. I fetched https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-4o on 2026-09-29; platform.openai.com/docs/guides/rate-limits redirects to developers.openai.com. Its table row reads "Tier 1 | 500 | 30,000 | 90,000" (RPM | TPM | batch queue).

REFUTED / CORRECTED:
(a) The 4.4–4.6 figure counts each verdict as prompt + 1000 (a reservation added on top of the prompt). The vendor page (developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/rate-limits, fetched 2026-09-29) says something different: "Your rate limit is calculated as the maximum of `max_tokens` and the estimated number of tokens based on the character count of your request." Read literally, that is a maximum, not a sum. With a 5.5–5.9k prompt the max_tokens=1000 term drops out. The vendor-backed ceiling is then 30,000 ÷ 5,498–5,942 ≈ 5.0–5.5 verdicts/min. That is roughly the doc's own "5.2/min if the reservation premise is discarded". One caveat: OpenAI's estimate is based on character count, not tokeniser count, so the real charge may differ a little.
(b) The arithmetic under the doc's own sum premise is also off. 5,942 + 1,000 = 6,942, not 6,800, and 30,000 ÷ 6,942 = 4.32. So the range is ~4.3–4.6, not 4.4–4.6.
(c) All throughput figures depend on the account actually being Tier 1, which has not been checked. They are modelled, not measured against a live account (doc lines 3-7).

No LLM API was called, no env var was read, and no Railway tool was used.
